RecGPT-100M is a 124.03M-parameter recursive causal language model trained for the BabyLM 2026 Strict track. It was trained for 10 epochs on a custom 100M-word English corpus using a 32,768-token BPE vocabulary.

The model applies a shared Transformer block recursively for 24 iterations. Its hidden size is 1,408, embedding size is 768, and feed-forward intermediate size is 22,528. Training used Aurora for the recursive block and AdamW for the embedding-related parameters, with a token batch size of 32,768 and sequence length 512.

A single-scale, attention-free Stream Mixer model featuring a 20-layer architecture with 8 parallel memory streams (dimension 32) and 8 sigmoid-gated read heads. Key improvements include a layer-wise dropout schedule (ramping from 0.02 in lower layers to 0.08 in deeper layers) and split path regularization (0.5x dropout rate for the recurrent mixer, 1.5x rate for the feedforward MLP blocks) to balance grammatical accuracy and semantic tracking. Children learn how to read letters before reading whole words, but we hide the character level information to our LMs behind opaque tokenizers.

This character level information could be useful to learn the morphology and relations among words: firefighter, grandmother, tree/trees, clear/unclear, play/played/playing. But LMs dob't have access to character level information, and to do so usually leads to architectural overburden. This handicap might be mitigated with gazillions of training data. But in low-resource settings, some words might be too infrequent for the model to learn.

Furthermore, this character level awareness could make the model more robust to casing and misspellings and we could help to answer how many "R"s are in "strawberry" more easily.

In this work I propose a new approach to allow the model to learn character level information during pre-training without any changes in the tokenizer or LM architecture, by adding the task of spelling. This could be done by an additional objective function and loss, but as prove of concept, for this work, it's done at input data level, were 1% of the words were spelled inline.

A decoder-only autoregressive Transformer (GPT-2 architecture) based on baseline BabyLM 2026 Challenge set-up. The model however use a different Tokenizer — MOP 16K (MorPiece) multilingual, actual vocabulary 39,697 (the "16K" label refers to the learned productive-segment inventory; the final vocab is inflated by CJK Hancharacter coverage injection and byte fallback). MoP's boundary-discovery mode is what distinguishes it from the BPE/Unigram baselines: instead of positing subword boundaries by merge frequency (BPE) or unigram likelihood (Unigram-LM), MOP segments by morphological productivity under Yang's Tolerance Principle — a candidate segmentation is admitted as a genuine morpheme boundary only when its exception count falls below the tolerance threshold O_N = N / In N, so boundaries track rule-like structure rather than corpus co-occurrence statistics. It applies CJK-safe pretokenization (with Han-coverage injection) so Chinese is segmented without whitespace assumptions, and exposes an order-of-acquisition (OOA) trajectory so segmentation granularity can be made to follow a developmental curve rather than being fixed.

Schedule is WSD (warmup 200 → constant peak 6e-4 → linear decay to 6e-5 over the last 25%); training stopped at exactly 100M reference tokens consumed (= 1 epoch, the BabyLM rule-cap milestone), well within the ≤10-epoch limit. Trained on 4× NVIDIA A10G in bf16 + 
 DDP with effective batch 131,072 tokens/step. The contribution is methodological (data-side ablation under a fixed-compute scaffold, with an audit-driven per-language data card that surfaces the register asymmetry across the three corpora — NL is 63% OpenSubtitles padding, ZH is 66% WenetSpeech subtitles), not architectural; this is the byte-premium-uniform zero-point of an ablation grid whose later cells attack data quality (category filtering, mixture reweighting, typological-bridge curricula).
